observations:
Torah #162 has zero bechina edges in the dataset. All package structure is derived from source-text analysis. After identifying all bechina-language nodes in the text, two packages are proposed in torah_162_packages.json: Package 1 (תּוֹרָה וּגְדֻלָּה — הַדָּרוֹם וְהַצָּפוֹן, 6 nodes, neutral polarity) and Package 2 (עֲנָוָה וְאַיִן, 3 nodes, good polarity). The new-package threshold is 3+ bechina-connected concepts forming an INDEPENDENT domain not yet represented by the proposed packages.

No candidate cluster meets this threshold beyond the two proposed packages:

1. The NARRATIVE DOMAIN (איש עשיר / מתנגד / ירידת נכסים): The story elements in line 1 (the wealthy opponent, his becoming pious, his declining wealth) are narrative illustrations of the teaching's point. None of these elements are given bechina-language identity declarations in the text. They cannot form a package because packages require bechina edges. The story IS the eitza dimension — it is a real-world instantiation of the conceptual tension, not a conceptual cluster of parallel-nature nodes.

2. The SPATIAL AXIS (דרום/צפון): These are already included in Package 1 as nodes. They do not form a separate independent domain — they are the spatial expressions of the Torah/greatness tension, not a new domain.

3. The EXEMPLAR DOMAIN (משה רבנו / רבנו הקדוש): The two historical figures cited with 'כְּגוֹן' at the end of line 3 are illustrative examples, not bechina-equated concepts. A bechina edge requires the text to say 'X IS a bechina of Y' — the formula 'כְּגוֹן' means 'such as' (an example), not 'IS.' Even if Moses and Rabbenu HaKadosh were treated as nodes, two examples cited with illustrative language do not constitute a bechina cluster. They would require explicit identity declarations (e.g., 'Moses IS a bechina of ayin') to be incorporated. The text does not provide this.

4. The NEGATIVE/EVIL DOMAIN (implicit): The structural negative pole — the person who IS 'somewhere' directionally, who is 'yesh' (something), who has an ego-position — is implied throughout the teaching but never articulated through bechina language. The text says nothing like 'גַּסּוּת הוּא בְּחִינַת הַיֵּשׁ' or 'יֵשׁ מַמָּשׁ הוּא בְּחִינַת X.' The negative pole exists only as a structural contrast — the teaching's problem-statement — without receiving its own bechina cluster. Therefore no evil-mirror package can be constituted. A possible third package (the 'yesh/ego' domain) would require the text to develop the negative side with parallel-nature declarations, which it does not do.

5. The COEXISTENCE DOMAIN (תורה וגדולה במקום אחד): The resolution state — Torah and greatness coexisting — appears in line 3 but only as a result-statement with 'עַל כֵּן' (therefore), making it an eitza-outcome of being in the ayin-state. It is not a new bechina cluster; it is the causal consequence that Package 2 (ayin) produces with respect to Package 1. Packages are built from bechina (parallel nature), not from eitza outcomes.

Conclusion: Torah #162 is a self-contained teaching with a clean two-package bechina structure. The brevity of the text (3 lines, approximately 120 Hebrew words) naturally limits the bechina topology. The two proposed packages fully exhaust the bechina-language content of the source text. No domain with 3+ independent bechina-connected nodes exists beyond what Packages 1 and 2 already capture.
